Microsoft Patches RoguePlanet Defender Flaw That Can Grant SYSTEM Privileges

The Hacker NewsBleepingComputer
2026-07-09 9 use cases 3 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft has released security updates for a Defender vulnerability known as RoguePlanet, nearly a month after details of the flaw became public. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-50656 (CVSS score: 7.8), is a privilege escalation issue in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine ("mpengine.dll"), which provides scanning, detection, and cleaning capabilities for its antivirus and

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Microsoft Defender engine (MsMpEng.exe) spawns interactive shell as SYSTEM - RoguePlanet CVE-2026-50656 AIExploitation High
Hunts the RoguePlanet exploit's runtime signature: the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine process (MsMpEng.exe / mpengine.dll) winning a TOCTOU race and spawning a command shell or script host running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. MsMpEng.exe legitimately only spawns MpCmdRun.exe, so any cmd/powershell/LOLBin child is a near-certain exploitation of CVE-2026-50656. Rationale: Pivots on the exact parent-child relationship named in the kill-chain (InitiatingProcessFileName MsMpEng.exe spawning cmd/powershell as SYSTEM). Second-sourced via Morphisec/Kudelski confirming the engine runs as SYSTEM with legit parent services.exe and only spawns MpCmdRun.exe, making shell children high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50656 • https://www.morphisec.com/blog/microsoft-defender-zero-day-rogueplanet-when-your-detector-becomes-the-attack-surface/ • https://kudelskisecurity.com/research/rogueplanet-zero-day-ms-defender-privilege-escalation • https://threatprotect.qualys.com/2026/06/18/microsoft-defender-zero-day-vulnerability-exploited-in-attacks-cve-2026-50656-rogueplanet/
ATT&CKT1068 T1211 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender Troubleshooting Mode sessions where an admin interacts with the engine (verify InitiatingProcessParentFileName and an active support case)
  • Security-vendor QA / red-team validation of the RoguePlanet PoC in a sanctioned lab
  • EDR sensor mislabeling MpCmdRun.exe path in rare AV-update races (validate the child is genuinely cmd/powershell, not MpCmdRun.exe)
  • Third-party AV/EDR that renames its own scan process to MsMpEng.exe (confirm SHA256 / signer is Microsoft)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Windows Defender\Platform\" and not (ProcessCommandLine has "MpCmdRun")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the child's parent is genuinely the Defender engine — validate InitiatingProcessSHA256 signer is Microsoft and folder path is %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Platform\*. Pull ChildCmd and integrity level; a SYSTEM cmd/powershell with a real command line = confirmed exploit. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host, kill the child process tree, and force a Defender platform/engine update to >=1.1.26060.3008; capture volatile memory first if IR requires. 3) HUNT: Enumerate all subsequent SYSTEM processes on the host in the 10 minutes after the shell, check for new local admin accounts (4720/4732), service installs, and lateral auth from this host; sweep the fleet with the vulnerable-engine UC.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "MsMpEng.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentPath    = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ChildProcess  = FileName,
          ChildCmd      = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildIntegrity= ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ChildTokenElevation = ProcessTokenElevation,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\MsMpEng.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\cmd.exe", @"\powershell.exe", @"\pwsh.exe", @"\wscript.exe", @"\cscript.exe", @"\mshta.exe", @"\rundll32.exe", @"\regsvr32.exe", @"\net.exe", @"\whoami.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Defender Engine MsMpEng.exe Spawning Interactive Shell (RoguePlanet CVE-2026-50656)
id: 7f3c9e42-1a6b-4d2e-9c80-2b5a0f8e1d34
description: Detects the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine process (MsMpEng.exe) spawning a command shell or script host, the runtime signature of RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656) privilege escalation to SYSTEM. MsMpEng.exe legitimately spawns only MpCmdRun.exe.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/microsoft-patches-rogueplanet-defender.html
  - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50656
  - https://www.morphisec.com/blog/microsoft-defender-zero-day-rogueplanet-when-your-detector-becomes-the-attack-surface/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1211
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\MsMpEng.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - No known legitimate scenario; MsMpEng.exe does not spawn interactive shells
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\MsMpEng.exe OR *\\msmpeng.exe OR *\\MSMPENG.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\whoami.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/MsMpEng\.exe/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|net|whoami)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, IntegrityLevel], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true allow_old_summaries=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="MsMpEng.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_integrity_level | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false allow_old_summaries=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="MsMpEng.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_integrity_level | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Vulnerable Microsoft Malware Protection Engine below 1.1.26060.3008 - RoguePlanet CVE-2026-50656 exposure AIWeaponization High
Surfaces endpoints still running a Microsoft Malware Protection Engine build vulnerable to RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656), i.e. any engine older than the fixed 1.1.26060.3008. The exploit succeeds on fully patched Windows regardless of real-time protection state, so unpatched engine version is the primary exposure signal. Rationale: Uses the concrete fixed engine build named in the article (1.1.26060.3008) mapped to CVE-2026-50656; TVM/Vulnerabilities inventory is the cleanest fleet-wide exposure pivot. Cross-checked against MSRC advisory which confirms the CVE and remediated engine version. Cross-checked against: • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50656 • https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-50656
ATT&CKT1211 T1068
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Air-gapped / offline hosts with stale TVM inventory that already updated the engine but haven't reported in (correlate with last-seen)
  • Devices where Defender is not the active AV (engine present but dormant) — lower practical risk but still flagged
  • TVM lag: engine auto-updated within hours but the daily vulnerability snapshot not yet refreshed
  • Non-persistent VDI images rebuilt from an old golden image each boot (fix the base image, not each clone)
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Rank flagged devices by internet-exposure and privileged-user presence; confirm SoftwareVersion is genuinely < 1.1.26060.3008 and not a reporting lag by checking device last-seen. 2) CONTAIN: Trigger a manual Defender security-intelligence/platform update (`MpCmdRun.exe -SignatureUpdate` or Intune remediation) to force engine >=1.1.26060.3008; prioritize crown-jewel and multi-user hosts. 3) HUNT: On any still-vulnerable host, run the MsMpEng.exe-shell UC over the last 30 days to detect prior exploitation, and check for unexplained SYSTEM processes or new privileged accounts.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-50656"
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-50656"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true allow_old_summaries=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-50656" by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.cve | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false allow_old_summaries=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-50656" by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.cve | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry

status: experimental

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50656", "CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-41091")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50656", "CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-41091")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/

    product: windows

    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Top AI Agents Built to Catch Malicious Code Can Be Tricked Into Running It

The Hacker News
2026-07-09 12 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Ask an AI coding agent to scan open-source code for security holes, and it might run the attacker's code on your own machine instead. That is the finding in a&nbsp;proof-of-concept published Wednesday&nbsp;by the AI Now Institute, an attack it calls "Friendly Fire." It works against Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex when either is running in an autonomous mode that approves its own

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] AI coding agent (Claude Code / Codex) executes README-suggested security.sh
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] security.sh launches hidden payload binary (code_policies) disguised as Go build · [LLM] AI coding agent lineage executing a local repo binary outside the standard toolchain · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Top AI Agents Built to Catch Malicious Code Can Be Tricked Into Running It
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
AI coding agent (Claude Code / Codex) executes README-suggested security.sh AIDelivery High
Hunts the Friendly Fire prompt-injection chain where an autonomous AI coding agent reads a poisoned README.md and runs the attacker-supplied security.sh check script. Article-specific because it pivots on the agent's own process (node/claude/codex) being the parent that launched security.sh, not a human shell. Rationale: Anchors on the exact bait script name 'security.sh' from the article's README code block, gated by the AI agent runtime (node/claude/codex) as the initiating process — human devs rarely run a repo's security.sh via the Node CLI. GitHub PoC (Boyan-MILANOV/friendly-fire-ai-agent-exploit) confirms security.sh is the injected wrapper. Cross-checked against: • https://ainowinstitute.org/publications/friendly-fire-exploit-brief • https://github.com/Boyan-MILANOV/friendly-fire-ai-agent-exploit
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A real repository legitimately ships a security.sh and a developer asks Claude Code to run it as an intended workflow
  • CI/CD wrapper invoking node that in turn calls a project's security.sh linting step
  • Security researcher intentionally reproducing the Friendly Fire PoC in a lab
  • Internal tooling that names its scanner script security.sh and is orchestrated by a Node-based agent
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ci","jenkins","github-actions") and DeviceName has_any ("build","ci","runner"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the event — confirm InitiatingProcess is an AI agent (node running claude-code/codex) and inspect what security.sh spawned next (look for an extensionless/hidden binary child). Read the repo's README.md for an injected 'Security testing' section urging pre-PR execution. 2) Contain: kill the agent + child processes, quarantine the repo working directory, and revoke any local secrets/tokens the agent had access to (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, cloud CLI creds). 3) Hunt: sweep other dev hosts for the same security.sh + agent-parent pattern and for the code_policies payload binary; check outbound connections from any child of security.sh.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "security.sh"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","claude","claude.exe","codex","codex.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude-code","@anthropic-ai/claude-code","@openai/codex","claude","codex")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "security.sh"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","claude","codex")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude","codex")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects an autonomous AI coding agent (Claude Code / OpenAI Codex, running as node/claude/codex) launching a security.sh script, matching the AI Now Friendly Fire prompt-injection RCE chain.
references:

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @CommandLine:*security.sh* (@ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\claude.exe OR *\codex.exe) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*claude* OR *codex*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/security\.sh/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|claude|codex)(\.exe)?$/i OR ParentCommandLine=/(claude|codex)/i

security.sh launches hidden payload binary (code_policies) disguised as Go build AIExploitation High
Hunts the second stage of Friendly Fire: the security.sh wrapper silently executing a pre-compiled binary that is disguised as the build output of a benign Go file. Article-specific because it pivots on security.sh as the parent spawning a non-shell, non-toolchain executable — the disguised code_policies payload. Rationale: Pivots on security.sh (article bait script) as parent while excluding the shell utilities it legitimately calls, surfacing the disguised payload binary. The corroborating GitHub PoC names it code_policies (decoy source code_policies.go), which the article describes as a binary seeded with strings from a harmless Go file to fool the agent's disassembly check. Cross-checked against: • https://ainowinstitute.org/publications/friendly-fire-exploit-brief • https://github.com/Boyan-MILANOV/friendly-fire-ai-agent-exploit
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate security.sh that compiles and runs a helper binary as part of a real scanning routine
  • security.sh invoking a locally-built Go tool (though 'go run' is excluded, a built ./tool would fire)
  • In-house SAST wrapper named security.sh that shells out to a proprietary scanner binary
  • Developer manually reproducing the Friendly Fire PoC
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("/usr/local/bin/","/opt/") and SHA256 in (dynamic([])))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the spawned binary's full path, SHA256, and signature status — an extensionless binary executing from a repo/clone directory with no build step is high-signal. Cross-check the hash against threat intel and whether a same-named .go source sits beside it (the decoy). 2) Contain: kill and quarantine the binary, isolate the host, and rotate any credentials reachable from the dev environment (cloud CLI tokens, SSH keys, package registry tokens). 3) Hunt: search for the same SHA256 / code_policies filename across the fleet and for any outbound network or file-write activity by children of security.sh on this host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "security.sh"
| where FileName !in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cat","ls","grep","egrep","awk","sed","echo","cut","tr","which","dirname","basename","env","go","gofmt","node")
| extend IsKnownPoCPayload = (FileName =~ "code_policies")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, IsKnownPoCPayload,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "security.sh"
| where TargetProcessName !in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cat","ls","grep","awk","sed","echo","cut","tr","which","dirname","basename","env","go","gofmt","node")
| extend IsKnownPoCPayload = (TargetProcessName =~ "code_policies")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, IsKnownPoCPayload
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AI coding agent lineage executing a local repo binary outside the standard toolchain AIExploitation Medium
Broader Friendly Fire hunt: any autonomous AI coding agent (Claude Code / Codex) that ends up executing a binary living in a project/clone directory rather than a system or package-manager path. Catches ports of the attack to projects other than geopy where the bait script/payload names differ from security.sh/code_policies. Rationale: Generalizes the Friendly Fire chain the article says 'ports to almost any project': the durable signal is an AI agent (node/claude/codex lineage) executing a binary from a repo working directory instead of a system/package path, which is how the disguised code_policies payload ran. Kept as hunting tier given breadth. Cross-checked against: • https://ainowinstitute.org/publications/friendly-fire-exploit-brief • https://github.com/Boyan-MILANOV/friendly-fire-ai-agent-exploit
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Agent running a project's own compiled helper/CLI from ./bin or ./target during a legitimate task
  • Locally built test harness or Makefile-produced binary executed by the agent
  • Language-specific project binaries (e.g. ./gradlew, ./mvnw, cargo-built tools) invoked under the agent
  • Developer using the agent to run a freshly built binary from the repo root
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("/target/","/build/","/dist/","/.bin/") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("build","compile","cargo","gradle","maven"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the executed binary was built locally (present in git as a pre-compiled artifact = suspicious; produced by a build step in the same session = likely benign). Inspect the README/docs the agent read for injected 'run this before PR' guidance. 2) Contain: if the binary was checked-in pre-compiled with no build provenance, kill/quarantine it, isolate the host, and rotate reachable secrets. 3) Hunt: pivot on the binary hash and on the agent-lineage pattern across all developer endpoints; review the source repo for a matching decoy source file (e.g. a .go/.py 'source' next to an extensionless binary) and for outbound connections the binary made.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","claude","claude.exe","codex","codex.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude-code","@anthropic-ai/claude-code","@openai/codex","codex")
| where FileName !in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","node","node.exe","git","git.exe","npm","npx","python","python3","go","gofmt","cat","ls","grep","awk","sed","env","which","cmd.exe","conhost.exe")
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/usr/" or FolderPath startswith "/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/sbin/"
    or FolderPath has "/node_modules/.bin/" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files" or FolderPath has @"\WindowsApps")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","claude","codex") or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude","codex")
| where TargetProcessName !in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","node","git","npm","npx","python","python3","go","gofmt","cat","ls","grep","awk","sed","env","which","cmd.exe","conhost.exe")
| where not (TargetProcessName has_any ("/usr/","/bin/","/sbin/","/node_modules/.bin/"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\claude.exe OR *\codex.exe) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*claude* OR *codex*)) -@Image:(*\sh.exe OR *\bash.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\git.exe OR *\python.exe OR *\go.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\conhost.exe) -@Image:(*\Program Files\* OR *\WindowsApps\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|claude|codex)(\.exe)?$/i OR ParentCommandLine=/(claude|codex)/i
| NOT (ImageFileName=/[\\\/](sh|bash|dash|zsh|node|git|npm|npx|python3?|go|gofmt|cat|ls|grep|awk|sed|env|which|cmd\.exe|conhost\.exe)$/i)
| NOT (ImageFileName=/[\\\/](usr|bin|sbin)[\\\/]/i)
| NOT regex("node_modules[\\\/]\.bin", field=ImageFileName)
| table([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData])

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GhostApproval Symlink Flaws Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code in AI Coding Agents

The Hacker News
2026-07-09 11 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Researchers at&nbsp;Wiz&nbsp;found that a flaw in six popular AI coding assistants lets a booby-trapped code project quietly take control of a developer's computer. The assistant asks permission to edit one harmless-looking file, but the write lands on a sensitive one instead. The affected tools are Amazon Q Developer, Anthropic's Claude Code, Augment, Cursor, Google Antigravity, and Windsurf.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Symlink created in repo pointing to SSH/AWS/shell files (GhostApproval staging)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Amazon Q / AI agent spawns shell child from poisoned .amazonq/mcp.json (CVE-2026-12957) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AI coding agent writes SSH authorized_keys or shell rc via GhostApproval symlink · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] SSH authorized_keys planted then remote SSH logon (GhostApproval key-injection use) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
AI coding agent writes SSH authorized_keys or shell rc via GhostApproval symlink AIInstallation High
Hunts the GhostApproval payload landing: an AI coding assistant process (Amazon Q, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Augment, Antigravity) creating or modifying ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or a shell startup file (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile) because a repo symlink named like a benign config file (project_settings.json) resolved to the sensitive target. This is the write that grants password-less SSH or arbitrary command execution on the next terminal. Rationale: Anchored on the exact GhostApproval targets confirmed by Wiz (~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.zshrc) and the six named agent processes; the pairing of a sensitive Unix dotfile write with an AI-agent initiating process is the specific, high-fidelity signal the article describes. Cross-checked Wiz blog and AWS bulletin. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/ghostapproval-a-trust-boundary-gap-in-ai-coding-assistants • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/2026-047-aws/
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1546.004 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • nvm / oh-my-zsh / starship installers spawned via node appending to ~/.zshrc during legit setup
  • A developer intentionally letting an agent add its own SSH key to authorized_keys for a remote dev container
  • Dotfile-manager tooling (chezmoi, yadm) launched from an IDE-embedded terminal running under node
  • Python-based provisioning scripts (Ansible local, pip post-install hooks) editing ~/.bashrc
  • IDE 'shell integration' features writing rc-file hooks on first launch
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("oh-my-zsh","nvm.sh","chezmoi","yadm","starship init") and FileName in~ (".zshrc",".bashrc"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and the parent repo path; open the target file and diff — a foreign ssh-rsa/ed25519 key in authorized_keys or an exported command / curl|bash line in .zshrc confirms it. Check whether the workspace was a freshly cloned/untrusted repo. 2) CONTAIN: Remove the injected key/line, rotate any exposed SSH keys, revoke the developer's active sessions, and quarantine the repo. If SSH is internet-reachable, block the host at the firewall until cleaned. 3) HUNT: Search all endpoints for the same agent process writing dotfiles; pivot to remote SSH logons on the host after the write and to any .amazonq/mcp.json in the repo.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName == "authorized_keys" and FolderPath has "/.ssh/")
    or FileName in~ (".zshrc",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile",".zshenv",".zprofile",".zlogin")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","code","Code.exe","cursor","Cursor","cursor.exe","windsurf","Windsurf","windsurf.exe","claude","antigravity","augment","python","python3")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("amazonq","amazon-q","language-server","cursor","windsurf","claude","augment","antigravity")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ssh-keygen","sshd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFileName == "authorized_keys" and TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/")
    or TargetFileName in~ (".zshrc",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile",".zshenv",".zprofile",".zlogin")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","code","cursor","windsurf","claude","antigravity","augment")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("amazonq","language-server","cursor","windsurf","claude","augment","antigravity")
| where ActingProcessName !has "ssh-keygen"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AI Coding Agent Writes SSH authorized_keys or Shell RC (GhostApproval)
id: 8f2c1a94-6b7e-4d21-9c3a-1e5f2a7b0c11
status: experimental
description: Detects an AI coding assistant process modifying ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or a shell startup file, the GhostApproval symlink payload landing.
references:
    - https://www.wiz.io/blog/ghostapproval-a-trust-boundary-gap-in-ai-coding-assistants
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ghostapproval-symlink-flaws-could-let.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1098.004
    - attack.t1546.004
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_target:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '/.ssh/authorized_keys'
            - '/.zshrc'
            - '/.bashrc'
            - '/.bash_profile'
            - '/.profile'
            - '/.zshenv'
    selection_agent:
        Image|contains:
            - 'node'
            - 'cursor'
            - 'windsurf'
            - 'claude'
            - 'antigravity'
            - 'augment'
            - 'amazonq'
    condition: selection_target and selection_agent
falsepositives:
    - Editor extensions or dotfile managers (nvm, oh-my-zsh) run through node that legitimately touch shell rc files
level: high
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/authorized_keys|\/\.zshrc|\/\.bashrc|\/\.bash_profile|\/\.profile|\/\.zshenv|\/\.zprofile)$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|code|cursor|windsurf|claude|antigravity|augment|amazonq)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/ssh-keygen/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified) AND (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zshrc" OR Filesystem.file_name=".bashrc" OR Filesystem.file_name=".bash_profile" OR Filesystem.file_name=".profile" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zshenv" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zprofile") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(process_name, "(?i)(node|code|cursor|windsurf|claude|antigravity|augment|amazonq)") | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(ssh-keygen|sshd)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified) AND (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zshrc" OR Filesystem.file_name=".bashrc" OR Filesystem.file_name=".bash_profile" OR Filesystem.file_name=".profile" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zshenv" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zprofile") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(process_name, "(?i)(node|code|cursor|windsurf|claude|antigravity|augment|amazonq)") | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(ssh-keygen|sshd)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Amazon Q / AI agent spawns shell child from poisoned .amazonq/mcp.json (CVE-2026-12957) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts CVE-2026-12957: a poisoned repo ships an .amazonq/mcp.json (or equivalent agent config) that Amazon Q auto-loads once the workspace is trusted, launching MCP-server processes that inherit the developer's AWS keys and can run commands. Detects an AI agent / language-server process spawning a shell or interpreter child that runs credential-touching commands (curl, chmod, base64, reads of ~/.aws). Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit CVE-2026-12957 detail (poisoned repo auto-loads a config file .amazonq/mcp.json and runs commands to steal AWS keys) plus the six named agent parents; requires the agent->shell->credential-command chain rather than bare agent-spawns-node so it stays hunting-grade. Cross-checked AWS bulletin 2026-047 and Wiz. Cross-checked against: • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/2026-047-aws/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/amazon-q-vulnerability
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1195.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate MCP server defined by a trusted repo shelling out to curl/pip during normal setup
  • Language-server post-install hooks running python/base64 for packaging
  • Developer-authored VS Code tasks that chmod +x build scripts
  • AI agent legitimately fetching a dependency via curl during a user-approved build
  • CI-runner style repos where node spawns bash for test bootstrap
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/build/","npm run","pytest","pip install") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pip install","npm") and not ProcessCommandLine has_any (".aws/credentials","authorized_keys"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Read the full ProcessCommandLine of the shell child and inspect the repo for .amazonq/mcp.json (or similar agent config) with an unexpected 'command'/'args'. Confirm whether ~/.aws/credentials was read or exfiltrated (network egress from the child). 2) CONTAIN: Kill the spawned process tree, rotate the developer's AWS keys and any cloud CLI tokens immediately, and revoke sessions. Update Amazon Q Language Server to >=1.69.0. 3) HUNT: Enumerate repos on the host for agent config files (.amazonq/mcp.json, mcp.json), review DeviceNetworkEvents from the agent for uploads to unfamiliar hosts, and check for the SSH-key / dotfile writes from the companion UCs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","code","Code.exe","cursor","Cursor","cursor.exe","windsurf","Windsurf","windsurf.exe","claude","antigravity","augment")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("amazonq","amazon-q","language-server",".amazonq/mcp.json","mcp.json")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","zsh","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","python","python3","osascript")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","chmod","base64",".aws/credentials",".aws\\credentials","authorized_keys","aws_access_key")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "mcp.json"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","code","cursor","windsurf","claude","antigravity","augment")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("amazonq","language-server","mcp.json")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash","/sh","zsh","dash","cmd.exe","powershell","pwsh","python","osascript")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","chmod","base64",".aws/credentials","authorized_keys","aws_access_key")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has "mcp.json"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AI Agent Spawns Shell From Poisoned MCP Config (CVE-2026-12957)
id: b3d47f60-2a19-4c88-8f0e-9d61c4a2ee73
status: experimental
description: Detects an AI coding agent or language-server process spawning a shell/interpreter child that runs credential-touching commands, consistent with auto-loaded .amazonq/mcp.json execution.
references:
    - https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/2026-047-aws/
    - https://www.wiz.io/blog/amazon-q-vulnerability
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - 'node'
            - 'cursor'
            - 'windsurf'
            - 'claude'
            - 'antigravity'
            - 'augment'
            - 'amazonq'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/bash'
            - '/sh'
            - '/zsh'
            - '/dash'
            - '/python3'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'curl'
            - 'wget'
            - 'chmod'
            - 'base64'
            - '.aws/credentials'
            - 'authorized_keys'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate MCP servers or agent build tasks that shell out to curl/pip during normal workspace setup
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(bash OR sh OR zsh OR dash OR python OR python3) AND @process.command_line:(*curl* OR *wget* OR *chmod* OR *base64* OR *.aws/credentials* OR *authorized_keys* OR *mcp.json*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(node|code|cursor|windsurf|claude|antigravity|augment|amazonq)/i
| ImageFileName=/(\/(bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|osascript)$|\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$)/i
| regex("(curl|wget|chmod|base64|authorized_keys|\\.aws/credentials|mcp\\.json)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","node.exe","code","Code.exe","cursor","windsurf","claude","antigravity","augment") OR Processes.parent_process="*amazonq*" OR Processes.parent_process="*mcp.json*" OR Processes.parent_process="*language-server*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","zsh","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","python","python3","osascript")) AND (Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*" OR Processes.process="*chmod*" OR Processes.process="*base64*" OR Processes.process="*.aws*" OR Processes.process="*authorized_keys*" OR Processes.parent_process="*mcp.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","node.exe","code","Code.exe","cursor","windsurf","claude","antigravity","augment") OR Processes.parent_process="*amazonq*" OR Processes.parent_process="*mcp.json*" OR Processes.parent_process="*language-server*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","zsh","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","python","python3","osascript")) AND (Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*" OR Processes.process="*chmod*" OR Processes.process="*base64*" OR Processes.process="*.aws*" OR Processes.process="*authorized_keys*" OR Processes.parent_process="*mcp.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
SSH authorized_keys planted then remote SSH logon (GhostApproval key-injection use) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Temporal correlation that catches the payoff of the GhostApproval SSH variant: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys is created/modified on a host, then a successful remote (network/SSH) logon occurs on the same host within an hour using the freshly planted key. Distinguishes a benign key add from an attacker immediately logging in. Rationale: Chains the two article-confirmed facts (agent writes into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, then 'they can log in with no password') into a time-window correlation so it only fires when the planted key is actually used remotely - far tighter than alerting on every authorized_keys edit. Corroborated by Wiz PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/ghostapproval-a-trust-boundary-gap-in-ai-coding-assistants
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1021.004 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin adds a legitimate key then immediately SSHes in to validate access
  • Configuration-management (Ansible/Salt) pushing authorized_keys followed by a scripted SSH health check
  • Cloud-init / provisioning that installs a key then the orchestrator connects
  • Jump-host onboarding where a new key and first login happen back to back
  • Backup/CI service accounts rotating keys and reconnecting
Suppression filter
| where KeyWriter !in~ ("sshd","cloud-init","ansible","salt-minion","puppet","cfn-init")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the process that wrote authorized_keys is an AI agent (KeyWriter field) rather than sshd/cloud-init/config-mgmt, and check whether the RemoteIP of the logon is expected for that user. 2) CONTAIN: If unexpected, kill the SSH session, remove the injected key, rotate credentials, and block the source IP; isolate the host if the repo is confirmed malicious. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the RemoteIP across the fleet for other SSH logons, review commands run in the session, and search other hosts for the same agent writing authorized_keys or .zshrc.
let win = 1h;
let keyWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName == "authorized_keys" and FolderPath has "/.ssh/"
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | project KeyWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where LogonType in ("Network","RemoteInteractive") or Protocol =~ "Ssh"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| join kind=inner keyWrites on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (KeyWriteTime .. KeyWriteTime + win)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, KeyWriteTime)
| project KeyWriteTime, LogonTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP, DelaySec, KeyWriter = InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by LogonTime desc
let win = 1h;
let keyWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFileName == "authorized_keys" and TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/"
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | project KeyWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ProcessName == "sshd" and SyslogMessage has "Accepted publickey"
| join kind=inner keyWrites on $left.Computer == $right.DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (KeyWriteTime .. KeyWriteTime + win)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, KeyWriteTime)
| project KeyWriteTime, LogonTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage, DelaySec, ActingProcessName
| order by LogonTime desc
source:linux.syslog @process.name:sshd "Accepted publickey"
#event_simpleName=UserLogon
| RemoteAddressIP4=*
| LogonType=/(3|10)/
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\/\.ssh\/authorized_keys$/i | rename(ContextImageFileName, as=KeyWriter)}, field=aid, include=[KeyWriter])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, RemoteAddressIP4, KeyWriter], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as KeyWriteTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" AND Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/*" AND (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=inner dest [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as LogonTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success AND (Authentication.app="sshd" OR Authentication.signature="ssh") by Authentication.dest Authentication.src Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where LogonTime >= KeyWriteTime AND LogonTime <= KeyWriteTime+3600 | eval DelaySec=LogonTime-KeyWriteTime | convert ctime(KeyWriteTime) ctime(LogonTime) | table dest process_name KeyWriteTime LogonTime DelaySec src user
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as KeyWriteTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" AND Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/*" AND (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as LogonTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success AND (Authentication.app="sshd" OR Authentication.signature="ssh") by Authentication.dest Authentication.src Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where LogonTime >= KeyWriteTime AND LogonTime <= KeyWriteTime+3600 | eval DelaySec=LogonTime-KeyWriteTime | convert ctime(KeyWriteTime) ctime(LogonTime) | table dest process_name KeyWriteTime LogonTime DelaySec src user
Symlink created in repo pointing to SSH/AWS/shell files (GhostApproval staging) AIWeaponization Low
Hunts the GhostApproval staging step: creation of a symbolic link (ln -s, mklink, New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink) whose link name masquerades as a benign project file (e.g. project_settings.json) but whose target is a sensitive out-of-repo path (~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.zshrc, ~/.aws/credentials, /etc). Catches attacker/CI/manual symlink planting; note git-checkout creates symlinks via syscall and is not covered by process telemetry. Rationale: Anchored on the exact PoC command Wiz published (ln -s ~/.ssh/authorized_keys project_settings.json) and the confirmed sensitive targets; requires the symlink target to be a sensitive out-of-repo path so it does not fire on ordinary symlinks. Low confidence flagged because git checkout plants symlinks via syscall (not ln) and won't appear here - it complements, not replaces, the file-write UC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/ghostapproval-a-trust-boundary-gap-in-ai-coding-assistants
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dotfile managers (chezmoi, stow, yadm) that symlink ~/.zshrc or ~/.ssh/config into a managed repo
  • Developer manually symlinking a shared .env or config into a project
  • Build scripts that symlink /etc/localtime or CA bundles into a container context
  • Homebrew/Nix post-install linking into the user profile
  • Test fixtures that create relative parent-traversal symlinks
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("chezmoi","stow","yadm","nix","brew") )
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Resolve the symlink target vs its name (readlink) and confirm the link name looks like an in-repo config (e.g. *.json/.env) while the target is a sensitive dotfile - a mismatch is the GhostApproval tell. Check the repo origin/trust. 2) CONTAIN: Delete the symlink before any agent 'sets up' the repo, and if an agent already ran, inspect the target file for injected content and remediate per the SSH/rc UC. 3) HUNT: Grep the repo tree for other symlinks resolving outside the workspace, and search the fleet for the same repo/URL and for agent processes writing authorized_keys/.zshrc.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "ln" and ProcessCommandLine has "-s")
    or (FileName in~ ("cmd.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "mklink")
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh") and ProcessCommandLine has "SymbolicLink")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("authorized_keys","/.ssh",".zshrc",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".aws","/etc/","System32","..\\..","../..")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where (TargetProcessName endswith "/ln" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "-s")
    or (TargetProcessName has "cmd.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "mklink")
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell","pwsh") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "SymbolicLink")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("authorized_keys","/.ssh",".zshrc",".bashrc",".aws","/etc/","System32","..\\..","../..")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Symlink Created Pointing to SSH/AWS/Shell Files (GhostApproval Staging)
id: 4a71e2c5-0d3b-4f19-a6c2-7b8e9f014d22
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a symbolic link whose target is a sensitive out-of-repo path, the GhostApproval symlink staging step.
references:
    - https://www.wiz.io/blog/ghostapproval-a-trust-boundary-gap-in-ai-coding-assistants
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ghostapproval-symlink-flaws-could-let.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1036.005
    - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_ln:
        Image|endswith: '/ln'
        CommandLine|contains: '-s'
    selection_target:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'authorized_keys'
            - '/.ssh'
            - '.zshrc'
            - '.bashrc'
            - '.aws'
            - '/etc/'
    condition: selection_ln and selection_target
falsepositives:
    - Dotfile managers or setup scripts that symlink ~/.zshrc or ~/.ssh/config into a repo intentionally
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:ln AND @process.command_line:*"-s"* AND @process.command_line:(*authorized_keys* OR *.zshrc* OR *.bashrc* OR *.ssh* OR *.aws* OR */etc/*)

| ImageFileName=/\/ln$/i

| regex("(authorized_keys|/\\.ssh|\\.zshrc|\\.bashrc|\\.aws|/etc/|System32|\\.\\.)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12958", "CVE-2026-50549", "CVE-2026-12957")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12958", "CVE-2026-50549", "CVE-2026-12957")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
